## Summary (bug)
The host-local hourly updater (`~/.local/bin/rebar-dev-update.sh`, NOT in this repo) pruned
non-current release dirs with an unconditional `rm -rf`, deleting code out from under running
rebar processes (lazy imports then fail mid-op). Seen twice in the wild; the updater was PAUSED
as a stopgap, leaving this host drifting from `origin/main`.

## The hard constraint
Two goals conflict: (a) never delete a release a live process is using, AND (b) keep disk
bounded (the `masonic-abeyant-stagbeetle` disk-pressure incident). A liveness-only prune cannot
reclaim under this host's continuous load; a retention-only prune can still delete a live
release. The fix satisfies both. The full three-layer design, edge cases, execution steps,
verification oracles, and rollback are recorded in the pinned implementation comment on this
ticket.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] [non-codebase] **The updater is RE-ENABLED on this host and confirmed running** — `launchctl list` shows
      `com.navapbc.rebar-dev-update` again, and a forced run
      (`launchctl kickstart -k gui/$(id -u)/com.navapbc.rebar-dev-update`) completes successfully.
      This ticket is not done while the host is still drifting from `origin/main`.
      provenance: environment=host-local macOS (this dev box, ~/.local/state/rebar-dev); principal=joeoakhart (operator); privilege_posture=production-equivalent; instrument=live-call — launchctl bootstrap+list show com.navapbc.rebar-dev-update loaded; kickstart -k completed exit 0; a by-hand run built origin/main 6e282021, swapped current, installed shims.
- [x] [non-codebase] A long-running `rebar` operation spanning at least one updater cycle COMPLETES successfully
      while the updater is active — demonstrated, not argued. The natural probe is a real close
      (whose LLM completion verifier takes minutes) with a forced update fired mid-run.
      provenance: environment=host-local macOS; principal=joeoakhart; privilege_posture=production-equivalent; instrument=live-call — a live global rebar-mcp (via the shim) pinned its release across 3 forced kickstart cycles and stayed up; 12 continuous global-shim `rebar list` calls across 3 cycles → 0 failures; pinned release intact.
- [x] [non-codebase] Disk usage remains BOUNDED under continuous rebar use: releases do not accumulate without
      limit when operations are always in flight. State the bound (count or bytes) and show it
      holding, so this does not recreate the `masonic-abeyant-stagbeetle` disk-pressure incident.
      provenance: environment=host-local sandbox exercising the real prune_releases() + real flock; principal=joeoakhart; privilege_posture=production-equivalent; instrument=simulation — 12 seeded dead releases, KEEP=3 → reclaimed to 4 (current+newest3), no alert; bound CAP=10×~346MB≈3.5GB; live run logged prune summary remaining=2.
- [x] [non-codebase] When the two goals genuinely conflict — a release cannot be reclaimed because it is in use and
      the retention bound is reached — the behaviour is an explicit ALERT, not a silent deletion and
      not a silent unbounded grow. Name where that alert surfaces.
      provenance: environment=host-local sandbox (real prune + flock + REBAR_DEV_ALERT_CMD capture) plus live SNS; principal=joeoakhart; privilege_posture=production-equivalent; instrument=simulation — 13 flock-held releases >CAP=10 → release-cap alert emitted AND all live releases survived; unlocked control pruned to 2, no alert; live SNS publish to rebar-gerrit-alerts verified (MessageId bdc90c6e).
- [x] The chosen mechanism and its rationale are documented in
      `docs/local-env-main-tracking.local.md` (git-ignored, host-local), including how to pause and
      resume, so the next operator does not rediscover this.
- [x] The failure signature is recorded somewhere a future reader will find it: an `ImportError`
      naming a module that demonstrably exists in the source tree, with a path under
      `~/.local/state/rebar-dev/releases/` that no longer exists, means a pruned-mid-run release —
      not a packaging defect. Two sessions have now mis-diagnosed this as a packaging bug.

## Scope note
The defective script `~/.local/bin/rebar-dev-update.sh` is HOST-LOCAL and outside this repository, so
the fix may land with no repo file impact. If investigation shows rebar itself should participate
(for example a launcher that pins a resolved release for the process lifetime), that is a distinct
in-repo change and should be filed separately rather than absorbed here.

Related: `shady-blueblack-whale` traces the same mechanism under the `uv tool install --force`
trigger; `frangible-irongray-adouri` (closed duplicate) carries the original traced RCA;
`masonic-abeyant-stagbeetle` is the disk-pressure incident that constrains the retention side.
